title: Google ML Kit
objectives: Understand Google ML Kit for Flutter via a real-life analogy
Pick the right sub-package: barcode / text / face / label / pose / translate / entity-extraction
Feed camera image streams to ML Kit efficiently
Fall back gracefully when service is unavailable

sections.markdown:
**Think of Google ML Kit as a bag of pre-trained micro-models Google ships to your phone.**

Run on-device, no server call, low latency, free. Each model is scoped to one task:

- **Barcode Scanning** — QR, DataMatrix, EAN, etc.
- **Text Recognition (OCR)** — printed + handwritten text; multiple scripts.
- **Face Detection** — bounding boxes, landmarks, contours, expressions, tracking.
- **Image Labeling** — 400+ common object labels.
- **Object Detection & Tracking** — bounding boxes for objects in a stream.
- **Pose Detection** — 33 body landmarks in real-time (fitness apps).
- **Language ID + Translation** — 100+ languages, on-device.
- **Entity Extraction** — dates, emails, addresses from text.
- **Smart Reply** — 3 short reply suggestions for chats.
- **Digital Ink Recognition** — handwritten strokes → text.
- **Selfie Segmentation** — mask around a person for background effects.

Each ships as a separate Flutter plugin under **`google_mlkit_*`** — smaller APK, faster init.

**Why every camera-heavy Flutter app leans on it:** you get Google-quality on-device CV without training a model, uploading images, or paying per-call. Vertex AI + Vision API charge per request; ML Kit is FREE. Cost is APK size (~5-40 MB per model) + accuracy that varies by task.

**Google ML Kit** is a set of on-device machine-learning APIs from Google. Flutter access via **`google_mlkit_*`** packages (one per task) or aggregate **`google_ml_kit`**. Uses **Google Play Services** on Android when available (small dynamic-download model), NNAPI + Core ML on iOS. Free at any volume. Complements **`mobile_scanner`** (specialized barcode) and heavier alternatives (**TFLite**, **MediaPipe**, **Vertex AI on-device / cloud**).

## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Wrong image format.** ML Kit expects NV21 / YUV_420_888 on Android and BGRA8888 on iOS. Wrong = garbage or crash.
**Mistake 2: No busy flag on frame handler.** Backlog fills up, memory spikes, UI jank.
**Mistake 3: Not `close()`-ing the recognizer.** Native resource leak.
**Mistake 4: Every model in one build.** Face + Text + Label + Translation = 60 MB APK bloat + slow install. Only install packages you actually use.
**Mistake 5: Google Play Services unavailable.** Non-GMS Android (Huawei / Amazon / offline emulators) may lack the ML modules; catch + fallback.
**Mistake 6: Doing heavy work on main isolate.** For batch OCR / big pipelines, offload to `Isolate.run`.
**Mistake 7: Rotation not set.** Portrait phone lens is rotated; without correct `InputImageRotation`, OCR fails.
**Mistake 8: Downloading translation model on cellular.** Translation pairs are 20 MB each; user may not want that on data. Add a Wi-Fi check.
## Best practices
**1. One package per task.** Don't bloat APK with modules you don't use.
**2. Correct `imageFormatGroup` + `InputImageRotation`.**
**3. Busy flag + throttle** on camera stream.
**4. `close()` recognizers in `dispose`.**
**5. Downloadable models on Wi-Fi** — check network status; explain data cost.
**6. Fallback UX** — 'ML Kit unavailable, tap to capture manually.'
**7. `Isolate.run` for batch / heavy pipelines.**
**8. Measure real device perf** — Pixel 7 vs entry-level Android differ 5-10× on inference latency.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Barcode scan via `google_mlkit_barcode_scanning` on a still image.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — OCR camera stream with busy-flag throttle.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Face detection with landmarks; overlay ovals + eyes.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — On-device translation en → hi with model download + Wi-Fi check.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Pose detection + fitness rep counter (squats).
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Multi-task pipeline: OCR + Entity Extraction → auto-fill a form with detected date, phone, email.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: When would you pick Google ML Kit over cloud vision APIs?**

**A:** **ML Kit wins when:** (1) latency matters — sub-100 ms inference; (2) offline required; (3) cost — free vs per-request billing on Vertex AI / Vision; (4) privacy — data never leaves the device (compliance + trust); (5) API rate limits don't apply. **Cloud (Vertex / Vision) wins when:** (1) accuracy for exotic cases (rare languages, complex diagrams); (2) custom domain-trained models; (3) OCR with layout preservation (Document AI); (4) large-batch offline processing on server. **Rule:** default to ML Kit; escalate to cloud only when accuracy demands it. Interviewer bonus: know that **Firebase ML (deprecated)** was the old story; migrate to standalone ML Kit + Vertex AI.

**Q2: How do you feed camera frames to ML Kit without jank?**

**A:** **(1) Choose the right imageFormatGroup on the CameraController** — NV21 (Android) / BGRA8888 (iOS). **(2) Busy flag** — `bool _busy = false;` skip frames while inference is running (drop-instead-of-queue). **(3) Throttle** — process 1 in N frames for less-critical tasks. **(4) `InputImage.fromBytes`** with correct rotation. **(5) Offload heavy pipelines to `Isolate.run`** — copies bytes to isolate, runs ML there. **(6) Native texture direct-access** on newer versions — some ML Kit APIs accept a native texture without copying bytes. **(7) `stopImageStream + startImageStream` toggling** — stop stream once you have your answer to save CPU. **(8) Measure with DevTools + real-device profile** — inference latency varies 5-10× across devices.

**Q3: How do you handle the APK size cost?**

**A:** ML Kit modules add real APK bloat: face detection ~10 MB, OCR per script 5-10 MB, translation per language pair 20 MB, pose 15 MB. **Options:** **(1) Only depend on packages you use** — a Flutter build with all ML Kit modules can approach 100 MB, hurting install rate. **(2) Play Services runtime downloads** — Android ML Kit downloads models via Play Services on first use (small initial APK, larger runtime). Called 'unbundled' models; recommended for size. **(3) Dynamic Delivery (Play Feature Delivery)** — install-on-demand for iOS+Android. **(4) Translation on-demand** — user must actively download language pairs; UX confirms Wi-Fi. **(5) Avoid iOS bundled models** — Play Services isn't there; iOS uses Core ML — bundled at build time. **(6) Post-install measurement** — Firebase Distribution + track APK size regression per release.

**Q4: What's the difference between ML Kit and TFLite / MediaPipe?**

**A:** **ML Kit** — pre-trained Google models via easy APIs; no ML knowledge needed. Fixed tasks (face detection, OCR). **TFLite** — deploy YOUR OWN trained models; full control, more setup. Use when Google's models don't fit (custom object detection, domain-specific classification). **MediaPipe** — Google's open-source multimodal ML pipeline framework; includes pose, hands, face mesh — sometimes overlaps with ML Kit but more customizable. **Vertex AI on-device** — deploy custom cloud-trained models to device via TFLite runtime. **When to graduate from ML Kit:** you need a task ML Kit doesn't cover, OR you need custom accuracy for a niche vertical (medical imaging, industrial inspection). Interviewer signal: knowing 'ML Kit is the easy default; TFLite is the escape hatch.'

**Q5: How does on-device translation work + when do you use it?**

**A:** **`google_mlkit_translation`** downloads language-pair models (~20 MB each) on demand + runs neural machine translation on-device. **Setup:** (1) Check if models are downloaded via `OnDeviceTranslatorModelManager`. (2) Download on user opt-in (with Wi-Fi warning). (3) Instantiate `OnDeviceTranslator(sourceLanguage: en, targetLanguage: hi)`. (4) `translator.translateText('Hello')`. (5) `close()` when done. **When on-device wins:** offline apps (travel, hospitality, medical translations without cellular), privacy (patient records), low latency (real-time subtitle overlay). **When cloud wins:** rare language pairs, better accuracy for context-heavy text, batch server-side workflows. **Cost:** free on-device; per-char cloud. **Interviewer bonus:** knowing on-device quality has closed the gap with cloud since ~2023; edge translation is production-ready for most consumer apps.

**Q6: How do you fall back gracefully when ML Kit is unavailable?**

**A:** Failure modes: (1) **Google Play Services missing** on Huawei / Amazon / OS-modified Android — Play-Services-based modules unavailable. (2) **Model download failed** (network / disk). (3) **Region restrictions** — some models are geo-limited. (4) **Runtime crash on old devices**. **Pattern:** (1) Wrap all ML Kit calls in try/catch; specific error codes exposed via `MLKitException`. (2) Feature-flag the ML-driven feature; on failure, degrade to manual entry / server-side call. (3) Detect Play Services availability at boot via `PlayServicesAvailability` (or an equivalent check); disable UI if unavailable. (4) Analytics on failure — measure impact per device / region. (5) Bundled fallback (iOS Vision framework alternatives, or a Firebase Function that runs cloud Vision API when ML Kit is unavailable). Interviewers respect the layered-fallback answer.

## Real-world usage

- **Barcode + OCR** — retail, logistics, ID capture.
- **Face detection** — profile photo cropping, filters, AR effects.
- **Pose detection** — fitness reps, yoga alignment.
- **Translation** — travel + hospitality apps.
- **Entity extraction** — auto-fill forms (dates, emails, addresses from OCR).
- **NOT ideal for** — custom domain models (use TFLite / Vertex AI); high-accuracy medical / industrial (specialized SDK).

## Advanced notes

- **`InputImage.fromBytes` vs `fromFilePath`** — file path for pre-captured; bytes for streaming.
- **Model manager APIs** — check downloaded / delete / re-download.
- **On-device model registry** — Play Services caches models across apps.
- **Custom text scripts** — separate models for Latin / Devanagari / CJK / Arabic; download the ones you need.
- **Barcode `getRawValue` vs `displayValue`** — differ for GS1 codes with special chars.
- **Face contour detection** — 133 landmarks vs 10; costs perf.
- **Face tracking** — assign IDs to faces across frames.
- **Smart Reply** — 3 short reply suggestions; consumer-messaging apps.
- **Selfie Segmentation** — mask for background blur / replace.
- **Digital Ink** — stylus input → recognized text; note-taking apps.
- **Pose landmarks 3D** — approximate depth (z) per landmark.
- **Vertex AI Studio** — bridge to hosted Gemini for tasks ML Kit can't do.
